name: Cat

app.note: The scale puts the standing ear tips 1.758 m above the floor, the ear tips of the red fox of the app, because the user chose the size of the fox on 2026-10-16 ("1.76 m, as the fox"). The leg factor 1.5 raised the ear tips from 1 to 1.0725 units, so the scale is 1.639161 m for each unit (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/arm-factors-legs.txt). The trunk factor lowers the ear tips 0.0641 units, and the longer legs of the trunk factor raise them by the same length, so the ear tips stay at 1.0725 units and the scale stays. The standing shoulder joints are 0.710693 units, 1.16494 m, above the floor (pnpm rig-mesh cat --check, docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-trunk/). At the shoulder joints of the parametric cat of main (0.55233 m), the cat was 0.868 m high to the ear tips (landmark-probe.txt). The reach is the reach of the red fox of the app, 0.5452 m from the left shoulder joint to the middle of the palm, because the user chose it on 2026-10-16 ("Fox reach"), as for the fox ("1.08x, rabbit reach"). The viola hold of the cat moves the viola back toward the neck until the left paw reaches the nut. With no --check, pnpm rig-mesh stops when the reach is more than 1% from this reach.

armFactorNote: The factor of the upper arm and the forearm that gives the reach of app.reach from the joints below at the scale of app.shoulders. pnpm rig-mesh cat --check measured 0.4791 m with no factor at this scale, so the factor of the reach of the red fox (0.5452 m) is 1.1496. The trunk factor and the longer legs keep the scale and the arms, so the factor stays (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-trunk/). With the leg factor 1 and the ear tips at 1.758 m, the factor was 1.0662, because the shorter body had a larger scale. At the shoulder joints of the parametric cat with the leg factor 1, the reach with no factor was 0.2538 m, and the factor of the reach of the red fox 2.2444 (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/arm-factors.txt, arm-factors-legs.txt).
legFactorNote: The factor of the thigh and the shin. Each one stretches only between its joints, the foot keeps its size, and the body rises 0.1365 units, so that the soles stay at y 0. The user chose the longer legs of the fox on 2026-10-16 ("Longer legs, 1.5x"): with the factor 1, the thigh was 0.075 units long and the seat 0.075 m high at the shoulder joints of the parametric cat. With the trunk factor, the legs grow until the standing ear tips stay at 1.758 m: 1.5 + (1 - trunkFactor) × 0.45 / 0.145 = 1.94168, where 0.45 units is the height of the neck joint above the hips joint and 0.145 units the height of the hip joint above the ankle (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cat-trunk.md).
trunkFactorNote: The factor of the trunk between the hips joint and the neck joint (trunk_moves() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The user said "the cat is too long and its chair is too low" on 2026-10-16, and chose the trunk of the red fox ("V2, fox trunk"): the standing trunk from the hips joint to the shoulder joints is 0.597 m, as on the red fox (0.698 m with the factor 1). The trunk keeps its width and its depth, and the cream belly becomes 14% shorter. The head, the arms, the legs, and the tail keep their sizes and move with the trunk. The factor 0.9 gave a trunk of 0.627 m and a seat of 0.238 m (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-trunk/).
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the pose of the source: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tips, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The probes are in docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/. sections.py gives the cuts at each height (sections-y.txt): the feet below y 0.04 (the toes forward to z 0.135), the thin shins from 0.045 to 0.105, the wide thighs from 0.11 to the crotch at 0.19, the body from 0.19 to 0.52 with the round belly forward to z 0.178, the shoulders from 0.525 (x ±0.172) to 0.655, the narrow neck at 0.685 to 0.705 (x ±0.06), the head from 0.705 with the muzzle to z 0.224, and the ears apart from 0.915. The trunk joints lie 0.01 to 0.02 behind the middle of the body cut, as in the fox, from the hips over the crotch to the chest 0.086 below the shoulder joint. The thigh joint lies at the crotch, a little behind the middle of the leg cut, the knee where the thin shin meets the wide thigh, the ankle where the foot starts, and the toes at the ball of the foot. The ear joint lies on the line of the middles of the ear cuts at 0.915 and 0.955, at the top of the head (0.89), and its tail at the ear tip. The cuts across the axis of the free arm (arm-axis.txt) give its middle line, which leaves the body between x 0.083 and 0.087. The shoulder joint lies on that line, 0.025 inside the root (x 0.06). The wrist lies at the narrowest cut, where the paw starts (s -0.02 to -0.01), the elbow halfway from the shoulder joint to the wrist and 0.01 behind the line, and the finger joint at the knuckles, 0.03 before the tip of the paw. The tail is a chain of two bones (sections-y.txt and sections-z.txt). The tail joint lies at the middle of the root of the tail, between its top on the back (y 0.35, z -0.04) and its bottom on the thighs (y 0.24, z -0.026). The tail hangs straight down to the bend at y 0.08, and its end goes back along the floor to the tip (y 0.03, z -0.215). The tail_tip joint lies at the bend, 0.223 units from the root. Each roll is the hint of the z axis of the bone, forward by default. The arm bones take the normal of the palm (palm): the smallest principal direction of the vertices of the left paw, inward and down (facts.txt).

studio.trunkNote: The trunk of the seated bind sits upright (trunk_turn() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py): the pelvis turns back around the head of the hips until the hip angle from the side opens by open degrees, and each trunk bone takes its share of that turn as its world turn. The trunk axis of the cat from the hip joints to the neck joint is vertical in the source. So with open 0, it leans 0.6 degrees forward in the play pose, and with open 3, the value of the red fox, it leans 2.4 degrees back (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/hip-probe-open0.txt and hip-probe-open3.txt). With open 1, it leans 0.4 degrees back (hip-probe.txt), and no face turns over after the crease. With open 0, the crease turned over 4 faces. The shares are the shares of the fox and the rabbit.

tailCurl.note: The seated tail curls on the seat around the left side of the haunch, on the side of the viola, as a sitting cat curls its tail (the variant T1 that the user chose on 2026-10-16, docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cat-seat.md). The points are the places of the curve after the root of the tail in the seated bind, in units from the root (curl_line() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py): down and to the left behind the haunch, forward along the left side of the haunch at the seat top, and the tip up and in over the left thigh. Each vertex moves by the smoothstep of its tail share from 0.5 to 0.95, so that the root of the tail stays with the haunch. The haunch is 18 to 21 cm wide on each side of the middle and the seat 21 cm, so the tail lies 11.8 cm outside the side edge of the seat at most. The tail goes 0.5 cm into the body at most, 0.1 cm into the left back post of the chair of the app, and 0.0 cm into the seat (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-seat/). The trunk factor lowers the root of the tail 1.3 cm closer to the seat top, and the tail goes 0.4 cm into the seat top in the rig, and 0.0 cm into the seat, 0.3 cm into the body, and 0.0 cm into the back posts in the app. A lift of the points by 0.0008 units or more raised the side view of the haunch from 0.13 cm to 1.9 cm (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-trunk/). Two straight bones cannot lie on the seat: the root bone is 36.6 cm long.

studio.note: The studio has no cat. legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind pose to the source, and the right side mirrors it. The seat is the seat of the fox and the rabbit (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-hip-open.md): the thigh slopes 15 degrees down from the hip to the knee, 8 degrees out, and the shin slants 23.8 degrees forward of vertical, so that the knee angle from the side is 128.9 degrees. The foot and the toes keep the turn of the source, so that the soles stand flat on the floor (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/leg_turns.py <config> 15 8 23.8, leg-turns.txt). The source shin slants 2.5 degrees back. With the leg factor 1.94168, the ankles are 9.0 cm in front of the knees, and the soles stand flat on the floor (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-trunk/seat-probe.txt). With the leg factor 1.5, the ankles were 7.0 cm in front of the knees (seat-probe-legs.txt). The bind arms are the bind arms of the fox and the rabbit. tailCurl gives the seated tail. With the hanging tail of tailBind (the root back over the seat 20 degrees below the level, the tip back and down behind the chair), the tail passed the back posts of the chair of the app and its end was 11.7 cm above the floor (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-mesh-cat.md).

weights.stretchRampNote: With a ramp, the upper arm stretches by the arm factor only on the free arm: the share of the stretch fades from 0 to 1 over this many units on each side of the plane |x| = armSplit. 0 gives no ramp, as for the fox and the rabbit.

sliver.note: The corners of each thin face share one set of weights, so that the face moves rigidly and does not turn over at a bent joint. A thin face has a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge below longest (units). The values are the values of the fox and the rabbit. The rule takes 177 faces in 16 groups (rig-mesh-cat-preview.log).

line.note: The middle corner of each long thin face (a corner angle above angle, in degrees) takes the mix of the weights of its two other corners by its place along their line, so that it does not lag behind the line when a joint bends. With head, the corners of the head take the rule too. The values are the values of the fox. The rule takes 172 corners.

weights.clavicleFromNote: The share of the clavicle weight that a vertex keeps grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height (units), and the chest takes the rest. This is the rule of the fox, moved with the clavicle joint of the cat (y 0.645 against 0.635), so that a small face of the chest does not take a clavicle weight that the bow arm turns far.
weights.armTopNote: The share of the weight of the clavicles and of the upper arms that a vertex keeps falls from 1 at the lower height to 0 at the upper height (units), and the neck takes the rest. The shoulders of the cat end at y 0.655, and the neck is narrowest at 0.685 to 0.705 (sections-y.txt). The rule of the fox keeps a raised bow arm from a drag of the side of the neck.
weights.shoulderRampNote: Above the heights of y (units), the share of the upper arm weight that a vertex keeps grows from 0 at the distance x[0] from the middle plane to 1 at x[1], and the clavicle of its side takes the rest. The cat has narrow shoulders under a thin neck, and bone heat gave 0.93 of the weight of vertices on top of the right shoulder next to the neck to the upper arm. Faces 187, 204, 205, and 250 from these vertices to the neck turned over in each sample of the violist (pnpm fold-probe violist). x starts at the neck (x 0.06) and ends past the root of the arm (x 0.087 to 0.13 in the cuts of sections-x.txt), and y starts at the top of the root of the arm. With this ramp, faces 187, 205, and 250 do not fold in the play, and the other faces of the top of the right shoulder fold in at most 18% of the play samples (face 162, docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/rig-mesh-check-cat-shoulder-ramp.log, hold-fit-violist-candidate.log). A lower armTop (0.6 to 0.66) gave the outer top of the shoulder to the neck, and a face there folded in each sample. A shoulder joint lower and further out (0.085 to 0.09 units out, 0.58 to 0.6 units up) folded other faces in each sample (rig-mesh-check-cat-fold-variants-1.log and -2.log, rig-mesh-check-cat-joint-variants.log).
weights.shoulderHeadNote: Below headFrom, the share of the head weight that goes to the neck grows from 0 at the smaller distance from the middle plane to all at the larger distance (units). The values are the values of the fox, scaled by the neck of the cat (x ±0.06 against ±0.089).
weights.fingersNote: The fingers keep this share of their bone heat weight, and the hand takes the rest, as in the fox and the rabbit.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the buttocks stay on the hips and the thigh turns onto the seat. This is the ramp of the fox (0.16 to 0.27), scaled by the thigh of the cat: it starts 0.025 units above the knee and ends 0.03 units above the thigh joint. The thigh of the cat is 0.075 units long, and the thigh of the fox 0.105.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones: the cuts of sections.py x show the arm apart from the body from x 0.087 out (sections-x.txt). Above headFrom, each vertex except the ears follows the head only: the neck is narrowest at y 0.685 to 0.705, and the chin starts at 0.705. The whiskers follow the head. Each ear vertex goes to its ear bone with a ramp over the heights of earBase. The tail has two bones (tail): the vertices within radius of the line from the root over the bend to the tip, and behind the plane z = behind, follow the tail bones. The share of the tail bones grows from 0 to 1 over the places of root along the line (units from the root), the share of the tip within the tail grows from 0 to 1 over bend units on each side of the bend, and the share of the tail bones takes the mean of its neighbors in smooth rounds. The radius holds each cut of the tail (x ±0.037 at most, facts.txt), and the plane keeps the backs of the thighs (z -0.025 at y 0.235) out of it. The rule takes 127 vertices, and 193 vertices have a tail weight after the smooth rounds.

refine.ringsNote: Each ring cuts the edges of an arm near a joint with the plane through the joint, as for the rabbit: joint (the arm bone that starts at the joint), minEdge (the shortest edge that the ring cuts, in units), and ends (the smallest part of the edge from each corner). The radius is 0.75 of the arm part that ends at the joint, so that it grows with the arm factor. With the arm factor 1.1496 and no rings, 4 long thin faces crossed the planes of the right elbow and of the wrists, and 1 face at the left elbow, 4 at the right elbow, and 22 at the wrists lay near the joints (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/rig-mesh-check-cat-rings.log). The rings at the elbows and the wrists cut 18 edges and add 36 faces. Three thin faces at the wrists stay across the plane with each ring of minEdge 0.04 to 0.08, ends 0.02 to 0.2, and a radius up to 0.15 units.

flip.note: The long edge of a face of the arms with a corner angle above angle (degrees) in the seated bind mesh flips to the corner of the face on its other side, when the two faces lie almost on one plane (normals, degrees) and the surface moves at most move (units). The values are the values of the fox and the rabbit. The rule flips 8 edges, with a move of at most 1.28 mm (rig-mesh-check-cat-final.log).

check.note: pnpm rig-mesh --check lists the faces of the seated bind mesh with a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge of at least length (units), when that edge passes within near (units) of a joint of the arms or the legs. These faces are candidates for a ring (refine.rings). The values are the values of the fox and the rabbit.

tone.note: The warm stage light gives the gray fur and the cream belly of the mesh four times the Oklab chroma of their faces: a front render of the gallery had the fur at chroma 0.061 and the belly at 0.065, against 0.016 and 0.020 on the sheet. The user chose the half step on 2026-10-16 ("Half step", docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cat-seat.md): each face of the plain fur moves half of the way of the full step, which gave the sheet medians in the gallery front. A row is [L, dL, da, db] in Oklab: the dark gray fur (L 0.49) gets 0.06 more lightness and moves toward blue, and the cream belly (L 0.87) moves toward blue. The gallery front then has the fur at L 0.486 and chroma 0.035, and the belly at L 0.802 and chroma 0.044. On the stage of the play frame, the fur looks neutral gray. The paws and the whiskers keep their colors, and the pink nose and inner ears have more chroma than 0.034 (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-seat/).

colors.note: Each face takes the mean sRGB color of the texture at the samples of a grid of the given steps on the face. A face is dark when its share of samples with a linear luminance below dark is at least eyeShare, and then it takes the mean of its dark samples. Each other face takes the mean of its samples that are not dark. A dark face in the eye box (the left eye at x 0.032 to 0.084, y 0.806 to 0.833 in the front view, mirrored for the right eye) is a face of an eye: 19 faces on the left and 25 on the right (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/head-colors.txt). A face in the nose box whose color is nearer to the nose color than to white is a face of the nose: the pink nose of the cat (19 faces at y 0.768 to 0.782, z 0.214 to 0.222) and its two dark nostrils. The box starts above the three dark faces of the mouth at y 0.752. The nose color is the mean of the pink faces. Then each face takes the nearest color of a palette of palette colors, from k-means in Oklab. The values of samples, palette, dark, and eyeShare are the values of the fox.

eyeShell.note: Each eye shell is a fan from the middle of the dark faces of the eye to at most this number of points of their edge, lifted this far (units) along the normal of the eye. pnpm studio-body finds each eye by its fan, drops the fan, and the app puts its pea eye there (design 4.5). The old eye is the dark faces and each face whose middle lies within reach times the radius of their edge, seen along the normal of the eye: 67 faces on the left and 66 on the right, with the few green faces of the irises. After the palette, the faces of the old eye take the color with the largest area in the ring of faces that share a corner with it: 50% of the area of the ring of the left eye and 41% of the right eye. Then each patch of dark faces near an old eye takes the color of its own ring. The cat has no such patch within darkReach: the nearest dark faces, the nostrils and the mouth, lie in front of the plane of the eye. The values are the values of the fox.

smooth.note: The big head of the cat hangs over its thin neck, and in the app the underside of the head faces down into the shadow of the head: a black band under the head from the back and the sides, and a thin dark line under the chin from the front. The face colors there are the cream and the gray of the fur, and a render with a flat light shows no line (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/chin-blender.webp). So the rig smooths the source inside the box before the weights, as for the dark band at the back of the neck of the fox: the neck and the bottom of the head from the back to the front of the neck (x from -0.12 to 0.12, y from 0.65 to 0.74, behind z 0.12). The chin, the jaw, the muzzle, and the eyes stay outside the box. Each vertex inside moves 0.5 of the way to the middle of its neighbors in 12 rounds: 34 vertices, at most 0.031 units. The head height H, the head center of the holds, the seat, and the footprint stay. A box to z 0.25 also smoothed the chin and changed H from 0.339 m to 0.352 m (rig-mesh-check-cat-smooth-1.log and -2.log).

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The half width holds the haunch of the cat (x ±0.14). The front edge ends where the thighs, which slope down, leave the seat top at the haunch. With the leg factor 1.94168, the shins start at z 0.197 units, the front edge of the seat of the app is 15.9 cm behind the back of the knees, the thighs over the front 10 cm of the seat are 0.1 cm above the seat top, and the back of the haunch is 1.2 cm in front of the back posts (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-trunk/seat-probe.txt). With the leg factor 1.5, the seat top stays at 0.216 units with the front edge from 0.08 to 0.1 units, and it falls 0.0013 units under the thighs with 0.11 and 0.12 units. The shins start at z 0.160 units (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/rig-mesh-check-cat-front.log), and the front edge of the seat of the app is 9.9 cm behind the back of the knees (seat-probe-legs.txt). With the leg factor 1, the front edge was 0.08 units (rig-mesh-check-cat-chair.log). The back edge keeps the back of the haunch 1.1 cm in front of the back posts of the chair of the app, as for the red fox (1.0 cm, seat-probe-legs.txt). The back edge of -0.111 units, the edge of the leg factor 1, kept it 5.0 cm in front. The seat of the app is 0.254 m high and 0.317 m deep (0.202 m and 0.316 m with the leg factor 1.5).

crease.note: The seated bind is smoothed across the crease where the belly meets the top of each thigh (crease_relax() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), with the values of the fox and the rabbit (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-hip-open.md). The seam has 15 vertices, 117 vertices move, at most 5.26 cm, and no face turns over (rig-mesh-check-cat-final.log). The corrective shapes give the source back, so the standing body keeps its form.

sit.note: The underside of the haunch behind the hip joints goes down onto the seat in the seated bind (sit() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The vertices at the root of the tail share their weight with the hips (0.45 to 0.51 of the tail), so with the values of the fox they moved by half of the drop, and the side view of the underside of the final bind stayed 5.22 cm above the seat. With root, a vertex counts its tail share only by its smoothstep from 0.7 to 0.95, so the root of the tail moves with the haunch. With no gap, a ramp of 0.015 units before the hip joints, a drop of at most 0.2 units, and 2 rounds of smoothing, the side view of the final bind was 1.93 cm above the seat at most with the hanging tail. The root of the hanging tail pulled a few vertices down and set the seat top, 0.2157 units. The curled tail does not pull them, and the seat top rose 0.8 to 1.2 cm, so top keeps it. With the curled tail of studio.tailCurl, the side view is 0.16 cm above the seat at most. With the trunk factor and the leg factor 1.94168, the seat top of the hanging tail is 0.2746 units, and the side view is 0.13 cm above the seat at most (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-trunk/). With the leg factor 1.5, the seat is 1 mm lower, the chair 2 mm deeper, and the standing body stays within 0.248 mm of the source. The red fox keeps 2.0 cm. The retro values gap 0 and ramp 0.015 alone gave 5.00 cm, and the haunch ramp 0.12 to 0.2 gave 5.40 cm (pnpm rig-mesh cat --check with these values as --set variants). The corrective shapes give the source back, so the standing body keeps its form.
